content.prompt:
You should spend about 20 minutes on this task.

Last month you stayed with an English-speaking friend for a few days. When you got home, you realised you had accidentally taken something that belongs to your friend.

Write a letter to your friend. In your letter

• apologise and explain what happened
• say how you will return the item
• thank your friend for letting you stay and invite them to visit you

Write at least 150 words.

You do NOT need to write any addresses.

Begin your letter as follows:

Dear …,
key_features: Informal, warm and natural tone: first name, contractions, friendly idiomatic phrases (e.g. 'I can't believe I did this!'), and an informal close such as 'Best wishes' or 'See you soon'.
Names the specific item and explains plausibly how it ended up in the writer's luggage, with a sincere apology.
Gives a clear, practical plan for returning it (e.g. sending it by courier this week with tracking, or bringing it on a planned visit) and when it should arrive.
Thanks the friend with specific details from the stay (places visited, a meal, their hospitality) rather than a generic thank-you.
Invites the friend to visit, suggesting a time and something they could do together.
Covers all three bullets with roughly equal development, at least 150 words, in clear paragraphs.
